title: How Long Equipment Rental and Demo Kit Has Been Back, and How the Amount Kept Back Is Taken
content:
A hold on an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement settled some days after the kit reached the counter is settled on a fuller record than one settled the same afternoon, and how the amount kept back is taken follows that gap and what the account shows was collected.

## The rule

Where the kit reached the counter at least 2 days before the hold is settled, and the rental account carries more than one payment collected against the agreement, the amount kept back is carried up to the whole dollar above.

Where the kit reached the counter at least 2 days before the hold is settled, and the rental account carries one payment or none against the agreement, the greater of the amount kept back and the assessments raised on the agreement is kept back, taken to the cent and never more than what the agreement still owes.

In any other case nothing under this heading changes how the amount kept back is taken.

## The two conditions in combination

| Days between the kit reaching the counter and the hold being settled | Payments collected against the agreement | How the amount kept back is taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or more | 2 or more | carried up to the whole dollar above |
| 2 or more | 1 or none | the greater of it and the assessments raised, to the cent, never more than what the agreement still owes |
| fewer than 2 | either way | nothing under this heading changes it |

The gap of 2 days is met by exactly 2 days and not by 1.

## Worked figures on a hypothetical settlement

Take an agreement where 220.25 USD would be kept back, whose account carries assessments of 300.00 USD raised on it and which still owes 400.00 USD.

- The kit reached the counter 4 days before the hold is settled and the account carries three payments: the amount kept back is carried up to the whole dollar above, which is 221.00 USD.
- The kit reached the counter 4 days before the hold is settled and the account carries one payment: the greater of 220.25 USD and 300.00 USD is 300.00 USD, which is below the 400.00 USD the agreement still owes, so 300.00 USD is kept back.
- The kit reached the counter on the same day the hold is settled: nothing under this heading changes how the amount kept back is taken.

Where the greater of the two would come to more than what the agreement still owes, it is what the agreement still owes that is kept back.

## Point of judgement

**Counting the payments.** What is counted is the payments collected against that agreement as its rental account records them; two or more is what the first row asks for.
